title: Club Membership: how the final late fee amount is finalized
content:
## Scope
This document states, for Club Membership, how the late fee's own repeat-delinquency-increased base amount and its capped employer-funded offset combine into the final billed late fee amount.

## Rule
The final late fee amount is the repeat-delinquency-increased base amount, less the capped employer-funded offset, rounded to 2 decimal places only at the end of the calculation, with no intermediate rounding. The final late fee amount is never billed as a negative figure.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose the repeat-delinquency-increased base amount is $22.50, the combined employer-funded percentage would otherwise take $9.00 off that amount, and the employer partnership tier's own annual wellness-reimbursement cap for this charge is $5.00. Because $9.00 exceeds the $5.00 cap, the capped offset actually applied is $5.00, not $9.00. The final late fee amount is $22.50 less $5.00, giving $17.50.

## Points of judgement
Where no employer-funded offset applies at all, the final late fee amount is simply the repeat-delinquency-increased base amount, rounded to 2 decimal places; where the capped offset happens to equal the entire repeat-delinquency-increased base amount, the final late fee amount is $0.00, never a negative figure.
